en.title: You Paid for a Service but Did Not Receive It
en.directAnswer: Keep the contract, advertisement, invoice, payment proof and promised service date. Ask the provider in writing to perform the service or explain the refund position. The Consumers’ Right Protection Act includes provisions relating to promised goods or services, but the correct remedy depends on the facts and the service.

atAGlance.whoFor: A consumer paid for a promised service that was not provided.

en.lawMeaning:
Do not promise a refund in every case. Contract terms and the law both matter.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Escalate through the correct consumer or sector route.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A training company cancels a paid course and offers no new date. Students should save the course advertisement and payment receipt before asking for a refund.
commonMistakes: accepting a different service without written agreement.
